verdict.rationale: Granola automatically generates enhanced notes once a call ends. Its default summarisation adapts to different meeting formats, and templates can shape the structure. Notes can be shared via a copy link, and community users report a reliably good summary. missing for 10: documented explicit key points/decisions/next-steps sections in the default summary output, and independent evidence that action items are captured reliably enough to share without editing (one PM reported action items slipping through).

support.subject: As a product manager, I get a structured summary right after each meeting — key points, decisions, and next steps — good enough to share without editing

citations.quote: Once Granola has recognised your call has ended, or you stop it manually, it will automatically generate enhanced notes.
While Granola's default summarisation adapts to a range of formats, you might want to choose a specific template (or set up your own!) for a specific type of call
Copy link will copy a unique URL link to the meeting notes, which you can send to others.
